instruction.german: Read the sentences in Figure it out. Then complete the rules in the grammar box with have to, must, mustn’t and don’t have to.

additionalAnswers.answer: don't have to and doesn't have to

parts:
Figure it out

Lucas works at an amusement park. He has to wear a special costume.

He must be friendly. He mustn’t take off the uniform in public.

He doesn’t have to talk to people or give information. It’s not necessary.

Does he have to wear the costume all the time? Yes, he does.


Grammar | Modal verbs of obligation and prohibition

We use must and have to to talk about obligation. Have to is more frequent than must when we speak.

• We use 1 to talk about prohibition.

• We use 2 and 3 to talk about when it’s necessary to do something.

• We use 4 to talk about when it’s not necessary to do something.

• We use 5 to ask about obligations.
